note: Ramond-Elliott syndrome involves dominant-negative TRA2B-3 isoform expression, and coloboma is a hallmark of overlapping conditions like CHARGE syndrome.

evidence.text: Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome is driven by a dominant-negative effect of the increased TRA2B-3 isoform rather than haploinsufficiency.

source.title: Entry - #621421 - RAMOND-ELLIOTT NEURODEVELOPMENTAL SYNDROME ...
source.quote: The findings suggested that the pathogenesis of the disease is not due to TRA2B haploinsufficiency, but rather due to increased levels of the TRA2B-3 isoform exerting a dominant-negative effect.

evidence.text: CHARGE syndrome prominently features uveal coloboma and related optic fissure closure defects within the MAC spectrum.

source.title: Genetics of syndromic ocular coloboma: CHARGE and ... - PMC
source.quote: Special attention will be given to two prominent, syndromic forms of coloboma, namely, CHARGE (Coloboma, Heart defect, Atresia choanae, Retarded growth and development, Genital hypoplasia, and Ear anomalies/deafness) and COACH (Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, Oligophrenia, Ataxia, Coloboma, and Hepatic fibrosis) syndromes.
